## Rationale

This is only applied on piped/grammar syntax pipelines. The functions you'll be using are the shared grammars and cannot be accessed with "eager form" syntax. Eager forms like `TTEST(<var_id>, <data>)` directly executes the outputs but cannot share grammars like `conclude()` and `tidy()` to retrieve the outputs. 

## Structure

The output from "eager form" syntax and output from the piped/grammar syntax have the same structure, only differs from their classes
